content_metadata.description: Jack Dorsey gives a presentation about his childhood obsession with maps and coding, detailing how these interests shaped his career.

qAndA.question: What city does Jack show a picture of at the beginning of his talk?

qAndA.answer: He enjoyed exploring them and imagining what was happening in different locations, using them as a tool for vicarious travel and understanding the world around him.
qAndA.question: Why was Jack so fascinated by maps?

qAndA.answer: A Macintosh, specifically referencing the year 1984 when the first Macintosh was released.
qAndA.question: What kind of computer did Jack's parents get when he was eight years old?

qAndA.answer: The ability to program and alter the computer, allowing him to bring his ideas and imagination to life.
qAndA.question: What specifically excited Jack about the Macintosh computer?

qAndA.answer: Both allowed him to explore systems, understand patterns, and engage his desire to visualize and create. Computers, however, offered the added dimension of real-time interaction and manipulation.
qAndA.question: What connection does Jack make between his interest in maps and his passion for computers?

youtube_description:
Excerpt:
Jack Dorsey, co-founder and chairman of Twitter, co-founder and CEO of Square, came to the Morningside campus of Columbia University on September 16, 2013. The iconic entrepreneur attracted over 1,000 Columbia students, alumni, and friends to the event in what proved to be the largest entrepreneurship event in Columbia history.Listen to his keynote address and find out how this young Missouri kid turned his obsession with urban maps, punk music, art, and coding into a micro blog that has quite literally changed the way the planet communicates.
youtube_title: Jack Dorsey on Living Vicariously through Maps
